la:verb:perrumpo.html:
per-rumpo, rūpi, ruptum, 3, v. n. and a.
, to break through.
Neutr., to break or rush through, to force one's way through: per medios hostes perrumpunt,: in vestibulum templi,: in urbem,: in triclinium usque,.—Impers. pass.: nec per castra eorum perrumpi ad Capuam posse,. —
Act.
In gen., to break through any thing: ut rates perrumperet,: perrumpitur concretus aër,: bipenni Limina,: laterum cratem,: costam,.—
In partic., to force one's way through any thing: paludem,: acie perruptā,; : perruptus hostis,: Acheronta,.—
Trop., to break through, break down, overcome: leges,: periculum,: quaestiones,: perrumpi affectu aliquo,: magistratus, qui te invito perrumpunt,overcome your modesty,: fastidia,.
la:verb:perrumpo.inflection: rūpi, ruptum, 3, v. n. and a.

la:adj:perrarus.html:
per-rārus, a, um, adj.,
very uncommon, very rare (as an adj. not in Cic.), : perrarum est, ut, etc.,.—Adv.: perrārō, very seldom, very rarely: si quando id efficit, quod perraro potest. ; ; : perraro haec alea fallit,.

la:adj:perreconditus.html:
per-rĕcondĭtus, a, um, adj.,
very hidden or abstruse, very recondite: ratio consuetudinis,.

la:adj:perridiculus.html:
per-rīdĭcŭlus, a, um, adj.,
very laughable, very ridiculous: doctrina,; .—Adv.: perrī-dĭcŭlē, very laughably, very ridiculously, : perridicule homines augurabantur, Zumpt, N. cr.
